title: In patients with recent minor noncardioembolic ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤3) or high-risk TIA (ABCD² ≥4), DAPT with aspirin plus clopidogrel should be initiated early (ideally within 12-24 h of symptom onset and at least within 7 days) and continued for 21-90 days, followed by single antiplatelet therapy, to reduce recurrent ischemic stroke.
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2021 Secondary Prevention (CHANCE, POINT); related trials: THALES (ticagrelor, separate IIb), INSPIRES (2023, post-guideline), CHANCE-2 (2021, post-guideline) · I/A

title: In spontaneous ICH requiring acute BP lowering, careful titration to achieve continuous, smooth, and sustained BP control, avoiding SBP peaks and large variability, can be beneficial to improve functional outcomes.
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2022 ICH Guideline; INTERACT3 (2023) · IIa/B-NR

title: In mild-to-moderate acute spontaneous ICH with presenting SBP 150-220 mmHg, targeting SBP 140 mmHg and maintaining 130-150 mmHg when appropriate is safe and may be reasonable.
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2022 ICH Guideline · IIb/B-R

title: In mild-to-moderate spontaneous ICH presenting with SBP >150 mmHg, acute lowering of SBP to <130 mmHg is potentially harmful.
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2022 ICH Guideline; ATACH-2 · III-harm/B-R

title: In warfarin-associated ICH with INR ≥2.0, give 4F-PCC dosed by INR/weight (recommended in preference to FFP) to rapidly correct the INR. Give IV vitamin K 10 mg directly after factor replacement to prevent INR rebound. 4F-PCC is preferred for rapid INR correction; this is not a claim of superiority for every clinical outcome.
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2022 ICH Guideline · I/B-R

title: IV thrombolysis can be beneficial (1) in unknown-onset stroke (e.g., wake-up) when treatment can start within 4.5 h of symptom recognition and MRI shows DWI-FLAIR mismatch (DWI lesion smaller than one-third of the MCA territory without marked FLAIR change), and (2) in patients ineligible for EVT who have salvageable penumbra on automated perfusion imaging 4.5-9 h from LKW or within 9 h of the midpoint of sleep for wake-up stroke. The pivotal trials (WAKE-UP, EXTEND) used alteplase; ESO 2023 expert consensus considers tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg a reasonable alternative for wake-up/unknown-onset stroke selected with advanced imaging.
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2026 AIS Guideline, section 4.6.3 recommendations 1–2, with July 2026 correction item 13; ESO 2023 expert consensus is separate · IIa/B-R

title: Tenecteplase (0.25 mg/kg, max 25 mg) is recommended as an alternative to alteplase (0.9 mg/kg, max 90 mg) for IV thrombolysis in eligible AIS within 4.5 h — either agent is first-line, and TNK is particularly practical when EVT is anticipated.
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2026 AIS Guideline; ESO 2023 (GRADE: strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence) · I/A

title: In patients with anterior-circulation proximal LVO (ICA or M1), NIHSS ≥6, prestroke mRS 0-1, and ASPECTS 3-5, EVT is recommended to improve functional outcomes within 6 h of onset and, in selected patients aged <80 without significant mass effect, at 6-24 h.
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2026 AIS Guideline · I/A

title: In carefully selected (e.g., milder severity) patients with AIS and atrial fibrillation, early oral anticoagulation is low risk and is reasonable compared with delayed anticoagulation (AHA/ASA 2026, COR IIa); the guideline notes that efficacy for preventing early recurrent stroke is not established. Supporting data: OPTIMAS (DOAC start ≤4 days non-inferior to 7-14 days for the 90-day composite) and the CATALYST IPD meta-analysis (≤4 vs ≥5 days: 30-day composite OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.50-0.98, no sICH excess).
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2026 AIS Guideline; OPTIMAS (2024); CATALYST IPDMA (2025); ELAN (2023); TIMING (2022) · IIa/A

title: In patients with AIS from anterior-circulation proximal LVO (ICA or M1) presenting 6-24 h from symptom onset with NIHSS ≥6, prestroke mRS 0-1, and ASPECTS ≥6, EVT is recommended to improve functional outcomes and reduce mortality. Perfusion imaging is not a prerequisite; adjunctive CTP or MRI (DWI-FLAIR mismatch or DWI-PWI) can be useful in EVT evaluation if immediately available (separate COR 2a, LOE A recommendation).
subtitle: AHA/ASA 2026 AIS Guideline; DAWN; DEFUSE-3 · I/A

title: For spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage associated with a factor Xa inhibitor, the 2026 NCS/SCCM focused update conditionally suggests 4-factor PCC rather than andexanet alfa (moderate-certainty evidence). Reverse promptly using the applicable local pathway, with monitoring for thrombotic complications.
subtitle: NCS/SCCM 2026 focused antithrombotic-reversal update, recommendation 1–1 · null/null

title: RESCUE BT2
subtitle: Favors tirofiban: 29.1% vs 22.2%

title: ATTRACTION
subtitle: MET superiority, favoring tirofiban: 49% (340/689) vs 43% (299/691)

title: RESCUE BT
subtitle: DID NOT meet superiority — neutral: median (IQR) 90-day mRS 3 (1-4) with tirofiban vs 3 (1-4) with placebo

title: MOST
subtitle: DID NOT meet superiority for either adjunct — mean (±SD) utility-weighted 90-day mRS 5.2±3.7 with argatroban, 6.3±3.2 with eptifibatide and 6.8±3.0 with placebo; both adjuncts were numerically WORSE than placebo

title: STRATEGY
subtitle: No significant difference: 17.1% vs 19.6%

title: ASSET-IT
subtitle: MET superiority, favoring tirofiban: 65.9% vs 54.9%

title: INSTANT
subtitle: MET superiority, favoring tirofiban: 63.8% (113/177) vs 52.2% (95/182)

title: DIRECT ANGIO
subtitle: No benefit: 36% vs 42%

title: EVA-TRISP prior-APT analysis
subtitle: Any previous APT associated with a shift toward LOWER mRS: OR 1.30; 90-day independence OR 1.62 (95% CI 1.22-2.16, p=0.001)

title: ESCAPE-NA1
subtitle: DID NOT meet: mRS 0-2 in 337/549 (61.4%) with nerinetide vs 329/556 (59.2%) with placebo

title: ESCAPE-NEXT
subtitle: DID NOT meet: mRS 0-2 in 206/454 (45%) with nerinetide vs 181/396 (46%) with placebo — no benefit, with the point estimate very slightly favouring placebo

title: ACTISAVE
subtitle: DID NOT meet: poor outcome in 21.6% with glenzocimab vs 15.3% with placebo — not significant, and the point estimate numerically favours placebo

title: TASTE (edaravone dexborneol)
subtitle: MET: mRS ≤1 in 67.18% with edaravone dexborneol vs 58.97% with edaravone alone — the combination was superior to edaravone alone

title: TASTE-2
subtitle: Nominally MET but only just: mRS 0-2 in 379/689 (55.0%) with edaravone dexborneol vs 333/671 (49.6%) with placebo; risk difference 5.4% (95% CI 0.1% to 10.7%). The lower bound of the risk-ratio confidence interval sits exactly at 1.00 and P=0.05, so this is a borderline rather than a robust result

title: EMPHASIS
subtitle: MET: mRS 0-1 in 447/850 (52.6%) with minocycline vs 403/851 (47.4%) with placebo — a 5.2 percentage-point absolute difference favouring minocycline

title: MIST-A
subtitle: DID NOT meet: median infarct growth ratio 1.8 (IQR 1.3-3.3) with minocycline vs 1.6 (IQR 1.2-2.8) with standard care — no reduction in infarct growth, with the point estimate numerically favouring the control arm

title: Y-6 phase 2
subtitle: No active arm significantly improved the primary endpoint; high/low-dose Y-6 44.6%/46.0% vs 35.7% placebo

title: OPENS-2
subtitle: MET superiority, favouring normobaric hyperoxia: median mRS 2 (IQR 1-4) vs 3 (IQR 1-4)

title: AVERROES
subtitle: Favored apixaban: 1.6%/y vs 3.7%/y

title: PRESTIGE-AF
subtitle: First events: ischemic stroke 1 versus 20; recurrent ICH 11 versus 1. All-event incidence rates are separate estimands: ischemic stroke 0.83 versus 8.60 and recurrent ICH 5.00 versus 0.82 per 100 patient-years.

title: ENRICH-AF
subtitle: Full efficacy not yet reported; the lobar-ICH subgroup was stopped by the DSMB for excess recurrent haemorrhagic stroke

title: SoSTART
subtitle: Inconclusive: 8/101 (8%) start vs 4/102 (4%) avoid; starting NOT shown non-inferior

title: APACHE-AF
subtitle: No difference: 26% (12.6%/y) apixaban vs 24% (11.9%/y) avoid; high absolute risk in both arms

title: COCROACH
subtitle: Favoured anticoagulation but non-significant: 14% vs 22%

title: ELAN
subtitle: 2.9% (early) vs 4.1% (later)

title: TIMING
subtitle: Non-inferior: 6.89% (early) vs 8.68% (delayed)

title: OPTIMAS
subtitle: Non-inferior: 3.3% vs 3.3%

title: CATALYST
subtitle: Favored early: 2.1% vs 3.0%

title: STABLED
subtitle: No reduction: 5.6% vs 4.9% per person-year

title: ISAT (18-year)
subtitle: Favors coiling: alive and independent more likely after coiling

title: CATIS
subtitle: NULL - the primary outcome DID NOT differ between groups: 683 events with antihypertensive treatment vs 681 events with control

title: CATIS-2
subtitle: Death or major disability: 289/2401 versus 250/2382 analyzed participants (12.0% versus 10.5%); randomized totals were 2413 and 2397.

title: ENOS
subtitle: NULL in BOTH comparisons - functional outcome DID NOT differ for glyceryl trinitrate versus none, nor for continuing versus stopping pre-stroke antihypertensives

title: COSSACS
subtitle: NULL - continuing antihypertensives DID NOT reduce death or dependency: 72/379 continue vs 82/384 stop

title: SCAST
subtitle: NEITHER co-primary favoured candesartan. The composite vascular endpoint did not differ (120 events candesartan vs 111 placebo). Functional outcome trended WORSE with candesartan, but the trend DID NOT clear the prespecified p≤0.025 threshold, so it is a signal rather than a demonstration of harm.

title: CHASE
subtitle: NULL - individualized lowering DID NOT significantly reduce poor outcome: 71.1% vs 73.4%. The point estimate numerically favours individualization but the confidence interval is wide and includes both meaningful benefit and meaningful harm.

title: Early AHT in AIS meta-analysis
subtitle: NULL on both primary outcomes - early antihypertensive therapy was NOT associated with a difference in all-cause mortality or in death/functional dependency

title: HOPE (reperfusion-guided BP)
subtitle: 60.0% versus reported 47.1%; 215 versus 225 analyzed. Control numerator is inconsistent: 106 in abstract/main versus 105 in Table 2.

title: ENCHANTED2/MT
subtitle: Favored less-intensive (worse with intensive)

title: OPTIMAL-BP
subtitle: Intensive worse: 39.4% vs 54.4%

title: BP-TARGET
subtitle: NULL - the intensive target DID NOT reduce radiographic intraparenchymal haemorrhage: 65/154 (42%) intensive vs 68/157 (43%) standard

title: BEST-II
subtitle: DID NOT meet the prespecified futility criteria. Mean follow-up infarct volume was 32.4 mL for the <140 mm Hg group, 50.7 mL for the <160 mm Hg group and 46.4 mL for the ≤180 mm Hg group - the MOST intensive arm had the SMALLEST infarct volume. Mean utility-weighted mRS was 0.51 (<140), 0.47 (<160) and 0.58 (≤180). This is a low probability of benefit, NOT demonstrated harm.

title: IDENTIFY
subtitle: NULL - intensive management to <130 mm Hg DID NOT improve outcomes: 130/183 (71.0%) intensive vs 135/200 (67.5%) standard

title: OPTIMAL-BP 1-year
subtitle: Functional independence at 1 year was NUMERICALLY LOWER with intensive management (40.5% vs 52.7%), but the INTENTION-TO-TREAT estimate did NOT cross conventional significance (P=0.051). Only the per-protocol analysis did (41.1% vs 54.7%, P=0.040). State this as persistence of the early signal, not as newly proven long-term harm, and never quote the per-protocol figure as if it were the intention-to-treat result.

title: Cochrane review: BP after reperfusion
subtitle: Intensive management results in LITTLE TO NO clinically meaningful difference in clinical function (high-certainty evidence). The review protocol defines the dichotomous clinical-function outcome on the mRS (0 to 2 favourable, 3 to 6 poor), and the plain-language summary reports it as the chance of living independently at about 3 months; read that way, RR 0.89 (95% CI 0.80 to 0.98) means slightly fewer patients were functionally independent with intensive lowering, a difference the authors judged not clinically meaningful.

title: ESPRIT (BP)
subtitle: Favors intensive: 9.7% vs 11.1%

title: BPROAD
subtitle: Favors intensive: 1.65 vs 2.09 events per 100 person-years

title: CRHCP 7-year follow-up
subtitle: 2.4% vs 3.0% per person-year

title: BRIDGE-TNK
subtitle: Favored TNK + thrombectomy: 52.9% vs 44.1%

title: IRIS IPD meta-analysis
subtitle: DID NOT establish non-inferiority of EVT alone: median mRS 3 (IQR 1-5) with EVT alone vs 2 (IQR 1-4) with IVT plus EVT. The CI crosses both the 0.82 non-inferiority boundary and 1.00, so this is an INDETERMINATE result — it neither establishes non-inferiority of skipping the lytic nor demonstrates superiority of bridging.

title: IRIS time-dependency analysis
subtitle: Statistically significant interaction: the benefit of adding IVT falls as the interval from onset to expected IVT lengthens. Adjusted common OR for a 1-step mRS shift toward improvement 1.49 at 1 hour, 1.25 at 2 hours, 1.04 at 3 hours.

title: DIRECT-MT
subtitle: Met its prespecified common-OR 0.80 noninferiority margin. This permits a 20% reduction in cumulative outcome odds, not a fixed 20% risk difference or a 20% loss of benefit versus no treatment.

title: SKIP
subtitle: DID NOT demonstrate non-inferiority: 60/101 (59.4%) with thrombectomy alone vs 59/103 (57.3%) with low-dose alteplase plus thrombectomy. The authors explicitly add that the wide confidence intervals also did NOT allow a conclusion of inferiority — an inconclusive trial, not a negative one.

title: DEVT
subtitle: MET the prespecified non-inferiority threshold: 63/116 (54.3%) with EVT alone vs 55/118 (46.6%) with combined treatment. The trial was STOPPED EARLY for efficacy after 234 of a planned 970 randomisations — 24% of the intended sample. The authors state the findings 'should be interpreted in the context of the clinical acceptability of the selected noninferiority threshold.'

title: MR CLEAN-NO IV
subtitle: DID NOT show either: median mRS 3 (IQR 2-5) with EVT alone vs 2 (IQR 2-5) with alteplase plus EVT. EVT alone was neither superior nor non-inferior — an indeterminate result on both prespecified questions.

title: SWIFT DIRECT
subtitle: DID NOT show non-inferiority: 114/201 (57%) with thrombectomy alone vs 135/207 (65%) with alteplase plus thrombectomy. The lower limit of the one-sided 95% CI was -15.1%, crossing the -12% margin.

title: DIRECT-SAFE
subtitle: DID NOT show non-inferiority of direct thrombectomy: 80/146 (55%) direct vs 89/147 (61%) bridging. The authors conclude the study should inform guidelines to recommend bridging therapy as standard treatment.

title: TNK-PLUS
subtitle: DID NOT meet superiority — a null result: 88/199 (44.2%) with tenecteplase before EVT vs 83/192 (43.2%) with EVT alone. Bridging tenecteplase did not improve clinical outcomes in the 4.5-24 h window.

title: ATTENTION LATE
subtitle: DID NOT show benefit (neutral result): 50/165 (30%) with tenecteplase before EVT vs 50/164 (30%) with EVT alone reached mRS 0-2. The authors conclude that adding IV tenecteplase before EVT did not improve functional outcomes compared with EVT alone.

title: Edinburgh CT criteria
subtitle: Excellent discrimination, confirmed on internal bootstrap validation. Of 110 participants, ICH was lobar in 62 (56%), deep in 41 (37%) and infratentorial in 7 (6%); of the 62 lobar haemorrhages, 36 (58%) had moderate or severe CAA and 26 (42%) absent or mild CAA.

title: Edinburgh criteria & ICH recurrence (IPD)
subtitle: Higher strata were associated with more recurrence. Primary 562-person analysis had 69 events over 1381 person-years: 48/307 in intermediate/high and 21/255 low. Reported five-year cumulative incidence was 16% versus 8%; these estimates are not simply the crude fractions.

title: RE-ALIGN
subtitle: STOPPED EARLY for harm after 252 patients, because of an excess of BOTH thromboembolic and bleeding events on dabigatran. Ischemic or unspecified stroke occurred in 9 dabigatran patients (5%) and in 0 warfarin patients; major bleeding in 7 (4%) vs 2 (2%). Dose adjustment or discontinuation of dabigatran was required in 52 of 162 patients (32%) to reach the trough target

title: PROACT Xa
subtitle: DID NOT meet non-inferiority and DID NOT meet the OPC success criterion. The trial was STOPPED EARLY after 863 participants because of an excess of thromboembolic events on apixaban. 26 primary events occurred: 20 events in 16 apixaban participants (4.2%/patient-year) vs 6 events in 6 warfarin participants (1.3%/patient-year)

title: BHF PROTECT-TAVI
subtitle: NEUTRAL - routine cerebral embolic protection DID NOT reduce stroke: 81 of 3795 (2.1%) with CEP vs 82 of 3799 (2.2%) without

title: PROTECTED TAVR
subtitle: DID NOT show a significant effect: 2.3% with CEP vs 2.9% without. The authors state explicitly that, on the basis of the 95% confidence interval, the result may NOT rule out a benefit of CEP - this is an indeterminate trial, not a demonstrated null

title: Warfarin resumption after ICH with a mechanical valve (meta-analysis)
subtitle: The abstract reports pooled rates of 5.23% for ischemic stroke off anticoagulation and 10.95% for recurrence after resumption. These are not directly comparable treatment effects. Recurrence counts and denominators conflict within the source, so no reconciled absolute recurrence count is asserted.

title: DOACs vs warfarin for LV thrombus (RCT meta-analysis)
subtitle: NEUTRAL at both timepoints - no significant difference between DOACs and warfarin: OR 1.69 at 1 month and OR 1.39 at 3 months. The authors conclude DOACs showed comparable efficacy and safety and are a reasonable alternative to warfarin, while calling for further large-scale trials

title: RIVAWAR
subtitle: 158/165 (95.8%) versus 84/87 (96.6%); imaging analysis excludes deaths. Met reported noninferiority criterion, not equivalence.

title: ARIES-HM3
subtitle: Placebo (aspirin avoidance) MET non-inferiority: 74% of the placebo group vs 68% of the aspirin group were alive and free of hemocompatibility events at 12 months

title: ELSO LV venting and acute brain injury
subtitle: Acute brain injury occurred in 525 of 13,276 patients (4.0%). LV-vented patients had HIGHER adjusted odds of acute brain injury (aOR 1.67) with NO difference in hospital mortality (aOR 1.07). In a propensity-matched comparison of the two venting strategies there was no difference between an intra-aortic balloon pump and a microaxial flow pump

title: CREST
subtitle: No significant difference: 7.2% vs 6.8%

title: CREST-2
subtitle: Stenting trial POSITIVE: 2.8% vs 6.0% medical alone. Endarterectomy trial NEUTRAL: 3.7% vs 5.3%

title: ECST-2
subtitle: No benefit from added revascularization in this low-to-intermediate-risk group

title: CADISS
subtitle: NO DIFFERENCE DETECTED, and the trial was far too small to detect one: stroke or death occurred in 3/126 (2%) assigned antiplatelet versus 1/124 (1%) assigned anticoagulant. Only 4 of all 250 patients (2%) had a recurrent stroke, all ipsilateral — an event rate far below what observational series had predicted.

title: TREAT-CAD
subtitle: DID NOT meet non-inferiority. The primary endpoint occurred in 21/91 (23%) on aspirin versus 12/82 (15%) on vitamin K antagonist; the upper bound of the confidence interval (21%) exceeded the 12% non-inferiority margin, so aspirin was NOT shown to be non-inferior. Note what this does and does not say: failing to show non-inferiority is not the same as showing inferiority.

title: CAD antithrombotic IPD meta-analysis
subtitle: DID NOT reach statistical significance: 3/218 (1.4%) with anticoagulation versus 10/226 (4.4%) with antiplatelet therapy. The direction favours anticoagulation and the point estimate is large, but with 13 events in total the confidence interval crosses 1 and the authors' own conclusion is that no significant difference was found in preventing early recurrent events.

title: STOP-CAD
subtitle: NO SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE in ischemic stroke: anticoagulation versus antiplatelet adjusted HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.45-1.12) by day 30 and 0.80 (95% CI 0.28-2.24) by day 180. Overall event rates were low — 162 new ischemic strokes (4.4%) and 28 major hemorrhages (0.8%) by day 180 — and 87.0% of all ischemic strokes had already occurred by day 30.

title: THEIA
subtitle: No significant benefit: 19/29 (66%) vs 13/27 (48%)

title: TenCRAOS
subtitle: No significant difference: 20% (8/40) vs 24% (9/38)

title: TO-ACT
subtitle: No benefit: mRS 0-1 at 12 months 67% vs 68%; halted after the first interim analysis for futility

title: ACTION-CVT
subtitle: Similar recurrence: aHR 0.94 (95% CI 0.51-1.73); major hemorrhage LOWER with DOACs: aHR 0.35 (0.15-0.82, p=0.02)

title: CHANCE
subtitle: Favored DAPT: 8.2% vs 11.7%

title: POINT
subtitle: Favored DAPT: 5.0% vs 6.5%

title: THALES
subtitle: Favored DAPT: 5.5% vs 6.6%

title: INSPIRES
subtitle: Favored DAPT: 7.3% vs 9.2%

title: CHANCE-2
subtitle: Favored ticagrelor: 6.0% vs 7.6%

title: TAPIS
subtitle: Higher with early DAPT: 68.7% vs 62.0%

title: IE baseline antithrombotic therapy and ICH
subtitle: Intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 182 of 3236 patients (5.6%), with the highest incidence in the combined-therapy group (9.5%) and the anticoagulation group (6.8%). Compared with no antithrombotic therapy, baseline ANTICOAGULATION was independently associated with more ICH (adjusted risk ratio 1.83), and COMBINED therapy carried the highest risk (aRR 2.45). ANTIPLATELET therapy alone was NOT associated with ICH, and ischemic stroke rates were similar across all groups

title: Thrombectomy for IE-related LVO (meta-analysis)
subtitle: Favourable outcome (mRS 0-2) at 90 days in 29.0% of patients, with successful recanalization (mTICI 2b-3) in 76.0%. Compared with non-IE large-vessel occlusion treated with thrombectomy, IE patients had a SIGNIFICANTLY LOWER rate of favourable outcome (RR 0.48) with no significant difference in any intracranial hemorrhage (RR 1.38, 95% CI 0.96-1.98)

title: COOPER
subtitle: One-month all-cause mortality was significantly higher among nonoperated than operated patients: 27% vs 5.9%. On multivariable analysis, heart failure, coma and cardiac surgery were independent predictors of mortality, with surgery protective (odds ratio 0.24). Neither the type of cerebral lesion nor the timing of surgery appeared to affect prognosis

title: IE-associated vs AF-associated stroke imaging phenotype
subtitle: IE-associated strokes were SMALLER (21.6 plus or minus 19.3 mm vs 66.9 plus or minus 38.0 mm), more often numerous (more than 10 lesions in 44.7% vs 5.2%), and far more often involved both anterior and posterior circulations bilaterally (54.1% vs 2.6%). Independent predictors of IE-associated stroke were younger age (OR 0.87), smaller lesion size (OR 0.94) and 3-territory involvement (OR 81.21)

title: NAVIGATE ESUS
subtitle: No benefit: 5.1%/yr vs 4.8%/yr

title: RE-SPECT ESUS
subtitle: No benefit: 4.1%/yr vs 4.8%/yr

title: ARCADIA
subtitle: No benefit: 4.4%/yr vs 4.4%/yr

title: SIESTA
subtitle: DID NOT meet superiority: general anesthesia NIHSS 16.8 at admission to 13.6 at 24 h (difference -3.2, 95% CI -5.6 to -0.8) vs conscious sedation 17.2 to 13.6 (difference -3.6, 95% CI -5.5 to -1.7)

title: GOLIATH
subtitle: DID NOT meet the prespecified hypothesis — the difference was not statistically significant, and the numerical direction favoured general anesthesia: median (IQR) growth 8.2 (2.2-38.6) mL with general anesthesia vs 19.4 (2.4-79.0) mL with conscious sedation

title: AnStroke
subtitle: NO DIFFERENCE: mRS 0-2 achieved by 19/45 (42.2%) with general anesthesia vs 18/45 (40.0%) with conscious sedation

title: CANVAS II
subtitle: NO SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE: functional independence 48.8% with general anesthesia vs 54.5% with conscious sedation

title: GA vs non-GA Bayesian meta-analysis
subtitle: Signal favouring general anesthesia, but the credible interval INCLUDES the null: OR 1.24 with a 94.2% posterior probability of superiority

title: BAOCHE
subtitle: Favored EVT: 46% vs 24%

title: BASICS
subtitle: NOT significant: 44.2% vs 37.7%

title: VERITAS
subtitle: POSITIVE: mRS 0-3 in 251/556 (45%) with endovascular therapy vs 128/432 (30%) with control

title: MR CLEAN
subtitle: Favored EVT; mRS 0-2: 32.6% vs 19.1% (absolute difference 13.5 pp, 95% CI 5.9-21.2)

title: ESCAPE
subtitle: Favored EVT; mRS 0-2: 53.0% vs 29.3% (p<0.001). Stopped early for efficacy

title: EXTEND-IA
subtitle: Both favored EVT: reperfusion median 100% vs 37% (p<0.001); early improvement 80% vs 37% (p=0.002). Stopped early for efficacy

title: SWIFT PRIME
subtitle: Favored EVT (p<0.001); mRS 0-2: 60% vs 35% (p<0.001). Stopped early for efficacy

title: REVASCAT
subtitle: Favored EVT; mRS 0-2: 43.7% vs 28.2% (adjusted OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.1-4.0)

title: HERMES
subtitle: Strongly favored EVT; NNT 2.6 to reduce disability by ≥1 mRS level

title: SELECT2
subtitle: Favored EVT (generalized OR 1.51)

title: ANGEL-ASPECT
subtitle: Favored EVT

title: RESCUE-Japan LIMIT
subtitle: 31.0% (EVT) vs 12.7% (control)

title: TENSION
subtitle: Favored EVT

title: LASTE
subtitle: Favored EVT (median mRS 4 vs 6)

title: ATLAS
subtitle: Favored EVT (median mRS 4 vs 5)

title: TESLA
subtitle: DID NOT meet superiority: UW-mRS 2.93 vs 2.27, adjusted difference 0.63 (95% CrI −0.09 to 1.34); posterior probability .96

title: TENSION antithrombotic analysis
subtitle: EVT benefit in every stratum: with antiplatelets cOR 2.40 (1.22-4.99), without 2.29 (1.53-3.46); with anticoagulation cOR 2.45 (1.17-5.28), without 2.12 (1.44-3.15); with IVT cOR 1.46 (0.83-2.61), without 2.89 (1.87-4.51)

title: LASTE ASPECTS 0-2
subtitle: Favored EVT: generalized OR 1.81; mRS 0-3 in 31.4% vs 8.5% (RR 3.69, 95% CI 1.77-7.68)

title: ANGEL-ASPECT HMCAS analysis
subtitle: No significant treatment-by-HMCAS interaction (p=0.19): EVT favored without HMCAS (generalized OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.80-4.27, p<0.001); not statistically significant with HMCAS (adjusted OR 1.69, 95% CI 0.93-3.08, p=0.09)

title: DAWN
subtitle: Favored EVT: 49% vs 13% (functional independence)

title: DEFUSE-3
subtitle: Favored EVT

title: MR CLEAN-LATE
subtitle: Favors EVT: median mRS 3 (IQR 2-5) vs 4 (IQR 2-6)

title: DISTAL
subtitle: No significant difference

title: ORIENTAL-MeVO
subtitle: Benefit: 58.6% (280 patients) vs 46.6% (283 patients)

title: DISCOUNT
subtitle: DID NOT meet its endpoint, with the point estimate favouring medical treatment alone: 72/116 (62%) with thrombectomy vs 81/119 (68%) with medical treatment alone. The trial was STOPPED at the planned interim analysis on the recommendation of the data and safety monitoring board for futility AND an increased rate of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage with thrombectomy.

title: ORIENTAL-MeVO ACAo Registry
subtitle: Favored EVT: adjusted OR 2.14 for the mRS shift; excellent outcome aRR 1.77 (95% CI 1.27-2.48); functional independence aRR 2.35 (95% CI 1.63-3.39)

title: ANGEL-REBOOT
subtitle: Neutral, numerically worse with bailout

title: PROTECT-MT
subtitle: WORSE with balloon guide catheter

title: ASTER
subtitle: DID NOT show a difference: 164/192 (85.4%) with contact aspiration vs 157/189 (83.1%) with stent retriever

title: COMPASS (thrombectomy)
subtitle: MET non-inferiority: mRS 0-2 in 69/134 (52%, 95% CI 43.8-60.3) with aspiration first pass vs 67/136 (50%, 95% CI 41.6-57.4) with stent retriever first line

title: ASTER2
subtitle: DID NOT differ significantly: 131/203 (64.5%) combined vs 117/202 (57.9%) stent retriever alone

title: VECTOR
subtitle: DID NOT differ significantly: 152/263 (58%) combined vs 135/258 (52%) contact aspiration alone

title: EXTEND
subtitle: Favored alteplase: 35.4% vs 29.5%

title: EPITHET
subtitle: Primary endpoint not met: infarct growth non-significantly lower with alteplase; reperfusion significantly more common

title: ECASS4-EXTEND
subtitle: Favored alteplase numerically; not statistically significant after early termination

title: TIMELESS
subtitle: Favored TNK numerically; primary endpoint did not reach significance overall

title: TRACE-III
subtitle: Favored TNK: 33.0% vs 24.2%

title: HOPE
subtitle: Favored alteplase: 40% vs 26%

title: EXPECTS
subtitle: Favored alteplase: 89.6% vs 72.6%

title: CHABLIS-T II
subtitle: 33.3% (37/111) vs 10.8% (12/113); no significant difference in 90-day clinical outcomes

title: TRACE-5
subtitle: POSITIVE: 83/221 (38%) with tenecteplase vs 66/231 (29%) with standard medical treatment

title: OPTION (TNK)
subtitle: Favoured tenecteplase: 123/282 (43.6%) vs 97/284 (34.2%) with standard medical treatment

title: OCEANIC-STROKE
subtitle: Lower with asundexian: 6.2% vs 8.4%

title: OCEANIC-AF
subtitle: Asundexian markedly WORSE: 1.3% (98 patients) vs 0.4% (26 patients)

title: AXIOMATIC-SSP
subtitle: Neutral prespecified dose-response analysis. Reported 16.8% placebo and 15.3–16.7% active-arm risks are model-based estimates, not raw event proportions.

title: SOUL
subtitle: MET superiority: 579 of 4825 (12.0%; 3.1 events per 100 person-years) with oral semaglutide vs 668 of 4825 (13.8%; 3.7 per 100 person-years) with placebo

title: SURPASS-CVOT
subtitle: MET non-inferiority but DID NOT meet superiority: 801 events (12.2%) with tirzepatide vs 862 (13.1%) with dulaglutide

title: Danish Hormonal Contraception Cohort
subtitle: Method-specific associations varied; progestin injection was inconclusive (RR 1.8, 95% CI 0.8–4.4). 4730 ischaemic strokes and 2072 myocardial infarctions occurred. Standardised ischaemic stroke rate per 100,000 person-years: 18 (95% CI 18 to 19) no use, 39 (36 to 42) combined oral contraception, 33 (25 to 44) progestin-only pills, 23 (17 to 29) intrauterine device. Combined oral contraception carried an adjusted rate ratio of 2.0 (1.9 to 2.2) for ischaemic stroke, equating to 21 (18 to 24) extra strokes per 100,000 person-years — a doubling of a small number.

title: Danish Progestogen-Only Contraceptive Cohort
subtitle: NULL against non-use: compared with non-use of hormonal contraception, NO progestogen-only method was associated with an increased adjusted incidence rate ratio for either ischemic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage. Against combined hormonal contraceptives containing ethinylestradiol, ischemic stroke rates were roughly halved: desogestrel-only pills IRR 0.56 and levonorgestrel IUD IRR 0.44.

title: CHOICE
subtitle: Favored alteplase: 59.0% (36/61) vs 40.4% (21/52)

title: CHOICE-2
subtitle: Higher with IA alteplase: 57.5% vs 42.5%

title: PEARL
subtitle: MET superiority, favoring IA alteplase: 44.8% (73/163) vs 30.2% (48/159)

title: ANGEL-TNK
subtitle: MET superiority, favoring IA tenecteplase: 40.5% (51/126) vs 26.4% (34/129)

title: IAT-TOP
subtitle: Superiority was not demonstrated: mRS 0-2 in 41.9% (52/124) with IA alteplase versus 46.7% (57/122) with control.

title: DATE (IA tenecteplase dose-escalation)
subtitle: Phase 1b: the 0.1250 mg/kg tier CROSSED the prespecified safety threshold (sICH in 3 of 12 patients, P=.04); sICH occurred in 1 of 14 at 0.0313 mg/kg and 2 of 22 at 0.0625 mg/kg. Phase 2a DID NOT demonstrate benefit at either surviving dose: mRS 0-1 33.8% (22/65) control vs 37.0% (17/46) at 0.0313 mg/kg vs 43.5% (20/46) at 0.0625 mg/kg

title: IA Thrombolysis Dose Network Meta-analysis
subtitle: Signal confined to two regimens: IA alteplase 0.225 mg/kg OR 1.94 vs control, and tenecteplase 0.125 mg/kg OR 1.90 vs control; lower-dose tenecteplase (0.0625 and 0.03125 mg/kg) and urokinase showed attenuated or uncertain effects

title: POST-TNK
subtitle: DID NOT meet superiority: 49.1% (132/269) vs 44.1% (119/270)

title: POST-UK
subtitle: DID NOT meet superiority: 45.1% (120/266) vs 40.2% (107/266)

title: ATTENTION-IA
subtitle: DID NOT meet superiority: 34.6% (36/104) vs 26.0% (27/104); adjusted absolute difference 8.3 percentage points (95% CI -3.8 to 20.4)

title: CASSISS
subtitle: No significant difference: 8.0% vs 7.2%

title: SAMMPRIS
subtitle: HARM from stenting: 30-day stroke/death 14.7% vs 5.8% (P=0.002); 1-year primary endpoint 20.0% vs 12.2%. Enrolment stopped early

title: ANNEXA-I
subtitle: Favored andexanet: 67.0% vs 53.1%

title: ANNEXA-4
subtitle: Anti-Xa activity reduced 92% (apixaban and rivaroxaban); excellent/good hemostasis 82% (204/249)

title: Andexanet vs 4F-PCC meta-analysis
subtitle: Hemostatic efficacy favored andexanet (RR 1.10). Primary overall mortality RR 0.72; 30-day mortality RR 0.82 was nonsignificant. Thromboembolic events were more frequent (RR 1.47). Different analysis sets and timepoints prevent treating differing significance as a logical contradiction.

title: INTERACT3
subtitle: Favored bundle

title: INTERACT2
subtitle: Negative primary: 52.0% vs 55.6%

title: ATACH-2
subtitle: No benefit: 38.7% vs 37.7%

title: INTERACT1-4 pooled
subtitle: Favoured intensive BP lowering: significantly decreased odds of poor physical function (mRS 3-6)

title: Deep vs lobar ICH BP meta-analysis
subtitle: DID NOT demonstrate a significant benefit of intensive BP reduction in either location. Step 1: deep OR 0.89, lobar OR 0.92. Step 2 (with INTERACT3 added): deep OR 0.82, lobar OR 0.97. All four confidence intervals cross 1.00.

title: TICH-2
subtitle: Neutral: no significant shift

title: FASTEST
subtitle: NEGATIVE: adjusted common OR 1.09; trial met prespecified futility criteria at 2nd interim analysis

title: STOP-MSU
subtitle: DID NOT reduce haematoma growth, and the point estimate favoured placebo: growth occurred in 43/101 (43%) assessable participants given tranexamic acid versus 37/97 (38%) given placebo

title: TRIDENT
subtitle: Lower with triple pill: 4.6% vs 7.4%

title: RESTART
subtitle: Fewer recurrences with antiplatelet therapy: 4% (12/268) vs 9% (23/268)

title: RECAP-ICH
subtitle: Reduced recurrent stroke: 96 (6.5%) of 1487 vs 152 (10.4%) of 1457

title: PEACH
subtitle: Favoured levetiracetam: a clinical or electrographic seizure occurred in 3/19 (16%) on levetiracetam versus 10/23 (43%) on placebo. Every seizure captured in the first 72 h was electrographic only — none were clinical.

title: ENRICH
subtitle: Favored surgery (posterior probability of superiority 0.981; prespecified threshold ≥0.975)

title: MISTIE III
subtitle: Negative: 45% vs 41%

title: MIND
subtitle: No significant benefit of surgery

title: SWITCH
subtitle: Favoured surgery numerically but not significant: 44% vs 58%

title: STICH
subtitle: Neutral: 26% vs 24% favourable

title: STICH II
subtitle: Neutral: unfavourable in 59% vs 62%

title: Hyponatremia & ICH
subtitle: Moderate 17.5% vs 13.3%; severe 18.7% vs 12.9%

title: CONVINCE
subtitle: Neutral: 9.8% vs 11.7% (3.32 vs 3.92 per 100 person-years)

title: CHANCE-3
subtitle: Neutral: 6.3% vs 6.5%

title: CLEAR SYNERGY (colchicine)
subtitle: Neutral: 9.1% vs 9.3%

title: Anti-inflammatory CV meta-analysis
subtitle: The effect on MACE VARIED BY DRUG CLASS rather than being uniform — driven by colchicine (RR 0.76, moderate certainty) and canakinumab (RR 0.88, moderate certainty), with NO benefit observed for other agents

title: CLEAR III
subtitle: Neutral: 48% vs 45%

title: LAAOS III
subtitle: Favors occlusion: 4.8% vs 7.0%

title: OPTION
subtitle: Safety superior — 8.5% vs 18.1%; efficacy non-inferior — 5.3% vs 5.8%

title: SPS3
subtitle: Neutral: 2.5%/y (DAPT) vs 2.7%/y (aspirin)

title: SSI antiplatelet network meta-analysis
subtitle: Cilostazol ranked best for preventing MACE (SUCRA 90.0%), reported by the authors as significantly better than aspirin, ticlopidine, dipyridamole, vorapaxar, sarpogrelate and placebo, although the ticlopidine comparison is borderline (95% CI upper bound 1.00)

title: VESALIUS-CV
subtitle: MET both primary end points. 3-point MACE in 336 patients (5-year KM 6.2%) with evolocumab vs 443 (8.0%) with placebo; 4-point MACE in 747 (13.4%) vs 907 (16.2%)

title: Ez-PAVE
subtitle: MET superiority: 100 events (Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidence 6.6%) with the <55 mg/dL target vs 147 events (9.7%) with the <70 mg/dL target

title: ROCATIS-1
subtitle: Reported change 54.4 vs 49.2; favored rosuvastatin

title: CHARM
subtitle: Neutral: no favourable mRS shift with glibenclamide (common OR 1.17, 95% CI 0.80-1.71; p=0.42); trial stopped early by the sponsor for slow COVID-era enrolment

title: DECIMAL
subtitle: mRS ≤3: 25% vs 5.6% at 6 mo (P=0.18); 50% vs 22.2% at 1 y (P=0.10) — underpowered; mortality reduced by 52.8 pp (P<0.0001)

title: DESTINY
subtitle: 30-day survival 88% vs 47% (P=0.02); mRS 0-3 at 6-12 mo: 47% vs 27% (P=0.23) — primary endpoint not significant alone

title: HAMLET
subtitle: No effect on primary outcome (ARR 0%, 95% CI −21 to 21); case fatality reduced (ARR 38%, 95% CI 15-60)

title: DESTINY II
subtitle: Favored surgery: 38% vs 18%

title: TEMPO-2
subtitle: No benefit: 72% (309/432) tenecteplase vs 75% (338/452) control

title: ARAMIS
subtitle: Non-inferior: 93.8% (DAPT) vs 91.4% (alteplase)

title: INTREPID
subtitle: Fever burden reduced: daily mean 0.37 vs 0.73 °C-hour

title: SETPOINT2
subtitle: No significant benefit: mRS 0-4 in 43.5% vs 47.1% (difference −3.6%, 95% CI −14.3% to 7.2%); wide CI cannot exclude clinically relevant benefit or harm

title: RAISE
subtitle: Superior: 79.5% (reteplase) vs 70.4% (alteplase)

title: Save ChildS
subtitle: Neurologic status improved: median PedNIHSS fell from 14.0 (IQR 9.2-20.0) at admission to 4.0 (IQR 2.0-7.3) at day 7. With no control arm, this is a description of outcome after treatment, not a treatment effect.

title: RESPECT
subtitle: Favored closure: 0.58 vs 1.07 per 100 pt-yr

title: CLOSE
subtitle: Favored closure: 0/238 vs 14/235

title: REDUCE
subtitle: Favored closure: 1.4% vs 5.4%

title: Finnish Subsequent-Pregnancy Cohort
subtitle: Women with a prior maternal ischemic stroke were LESS likely to have any subsequent pregnancy: 38.9% versus 51.7% of controls, age-adjusted OR 0.55. Among those who did conceive again, three women had a recurrent maternal ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack — reported as 8.6%, which is 3 events among the roughly 35 women who had a subsequent pregnancy, NOT 3 of 90. With three events, this figure is an order-of-magnitude estimate only.

title: INTERACT4
subtitle: Neutral overall: no difference in functional outcome

title: BEST-MSU
subtitle: Favors MSU: mean uw-mRS 0.72 vs 0.66

title: RACECAT
subtitle: Neutral: median mRS 3 in both arms

title: VNS-REHAB
subtitle: Favors paired VNS: FMA-UE +5.0 vs +2.4 points

title: RESIST
subtitle: DID NOT meet: median mRS 2 (IQR 1-3) with RIC vs 1 (IQR 1-3) with sham — RIC was not associated with improved functional outcome

title: RICAMIS
subtitle: MET: mRS 0-1 in 582 (67.4%) with RIC vs 566 (62.0%) with usual care — an absolute difference of 5.4 percentage points

title: SERIC-EVT
subtitle: MET: mRS 0-2 in 61.1% with RIC vs 48.9% with sham RIC — note that the effect estimate reported in the abstract is UNADJUSTED

title: EnTRIPS
subtitle: DID NOT meet: mRS 0-2 in 81/133 (60.9%) with RIPC vs 78/135 (57.8%) with control — no significant improvement in 90-day functional outcome

title: SAHaRA
subtitle: Neutral: 33.5% vs 37.7%

title: ULTRA
subtitle: Neutral: 60% vs 64%

title: EARLYDRAIN
subtitle: Favors lumbar drain: 32.6% vs 44.8%

title: ATIS-NVAF
subtitle: 17.8% versus 19.6%; stopped for futility

title: MATCH
subtitle: Neutral: 15.7% vs 16.7%

title: SAVE
subtitle: DID NOT meet: a primary end-point event occurred in 229 CPAP participants (17.0%) and 207 usual-care participants (15.4%) — the point estimate favors usual care

title: Post-stroke PAP meta-analysis
subtitle: PAP reduced recurrent vascular events

title: Suicide after stroke
subtitle: Higher in stroke survivors: 11.1 vs 3.2 per 10,000 person-years

title: QASC
subtitle: POSITIVE: intervention-unit patients were significantly less likely to be dead or dependent — 236/558 (42%) vs 259/449 (58%) — number needed to treat 6.4

title: CLOTS 3
subtitle: POSITIVE: proximal DVT in 122/1438 (8.5%) with IPC vs 174/1438 (12.1%) without — absolute risk reduction 3.6%

title: CLOTS 1
subtitle: DID NOT meet its aim — NULL: proximal DVT in 126/1256 (10.0%) with stockings vs 133/1262 (10.5%) without, a non-significant absolute risk reduction of 0.5%

title: PREVAIL
subtitle: POSITIVE for the composite: 68/666 (10%) with enoxaparin vs 121/669 (18%) with unfractionated heparin — a 43% relative reduction

title: FOOD (Trials 2 and 3)
subtitle: BOTH comparisons DID NOT meet significance on the primary endpoint. Trial 2 (early vs avoid): absolute reduction in death of 5.8% (p=0.09, not significant) but a reduction in death or poor outcome of only 1.2% (p=0.7) — i.e. the primary endpoint was flat, with the direction of effect being fewer deaths and more dependent survivors. Trial 3 (PEG vs nasogastric): absolute INCREASE in risk of death of 1.0% (p=0.9) and an increased risk of death or poor outcome of 7.8% (p=0.05), i.e. borderline evidence of harm from starting with PEG

title: SO2S
subtitle: DID NOT meet — NULL: no benefit of prophylactic oxygen at any dose or schedule. Unadjusted OR for a better outcome 0.97 for oxygen vs control, and 1.03 for continuous vs nocturnal oxygen. No subgroup could be identified that benefited

title: HeadPoST
subtitle: DID NOT meet — NULL: no significant shift in the 90-day mRS distribution between lying flat and sitting up

title: PASS
subtitle: DID NOT meet — NULL: preventive ceftriaxone did not affect the distribution of 90-day mRS scores

title: SHINE
subtitle: DID NOT meet — NULL, and enrolment was STOPPED FOR FUTILITY at a prespecified interim analysis: favourable outcome in 119/581 (20.5%) with intensive control vs 123/570 (21.6%) with standard control

title: AVERT dose-response
subtitle: The two dose dimensions pull in OPPOSITE directions: greater daily frequency of out-of-bed sessions improved the odds of a favourable outcome (OR 1.13), while greater amount of mobilisation in minutes per day REDUCED the odds of a good outcome (OR 0.94), each holding the other and time to first mobilisation constant

title: OPTIMISTmain
subtitle: BORDERLINE — non-inferiority NOT established with conventional confidence: mRS 2-6 in 809/2552 (31.7%) with low-intensity vs 606/1963 (30.9%) with standard monitoring. The upper 95% CI bound (1.15) reaches the 1.15 margin and p=0.057; the authors conclude only "weak evidence" that low-intensity monitoring is non-inferior

title: HeadSOAR
subtitle: DID NOT meet — no significant shift: median mRS 3 (IQR 1-5) with head elevation vs 3 (IQR 1-5) flat

title: ARTESiA
subtitle: Favored apixaban: 0.78%/y vs 1.24%/y

title: NOAH-AFNET 6
subtitle: Neutral: 3.2%/patient-year vs 4.0%/patient-year

title: LOOP
subtitle: Neutral: 4.5% vs 5.6%

title: GWTG-Stroke door-in-door-out
subtitle: Real-world practice falls well short of the benchmark: median door-in-door-out time 174 minutes (IQR 116-276), and only 29,741 of 108,913 patients (27.3%) were transferred within 120 minutes

title: Target Stroke Phase III
subtitle: Different strategies work at different points in the chain. In DIRECT-ARRIVING EVT patients, two strategies were independently associated with shorter door-to-puncture time: alerting the neurointerventional team on EMS prenotification (−21.9 minutes) and performing CT plus CTA in all patients presenting ≤24 h from last known well (−6.6 minutes). In TRANSFER-IN EVT patients, two different strategies helped: greater use of stroke screening tools (−3.5 minutes per 25% increase in use) and greater use of a camera during telestroke consultations (−5.8 minutes per 25% increase in camera use)

title: AI LVO-detection accuracy meta-analysis
subtitle: Sensitivity 0.87 and specificity 0.95. An absent AI flag cannot independently exclude LVO; performance and intended use vary by product and vessel territory.

title: CERES-TANDEM
subtitle: Emergent carotid stenting was ASSOCIATED WITH a better mRS shift after IPTW weighting

title: IRIS tandem-lesion carotid-stenting analysis
subtitle: Acute carotid stenting was ASSOCIATED WITH better 90-day functional outcomes; confirmed on inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting (adjusted common OR 1.66, 95% CI 1.08-2.54)

title: AcT
subtitle: Non-inferior: 36.9% (TNK) vs 34.8% (alteplase)

title: TRACE-2
subtitle: Non-inferior: 62% (439/705, TNK) vs 58% (405/696, alteplase)

title: ORIGINAL
subtitle: Non-inferior: 72.7% (532/732, TNK) vs 70.3% (515/733, alteplase)

title: TNK vs alteplase · RWE
subtitle: Source Table 2 reports 26/68 versus 122/303; matched-population interpretation is withheld because source cohort descriptions are inconsistent

title: TASTE
subtitle: Non-inferiority met per-protocol (59% vs 56%) but NOT in intention-to-treat (57% vs 55%)

title: T-FLAVOR
subtitle: Met its prespecified 90%-CI success criterion: 11/107 (10.3%) with tenecteplase vs 4/111 (3.6%) with low-dose alteplase. The authors state that the conventional 95% CI (-0.19% to 13.2%) crosses zero, so the result is NOT significant at the usual 0.05 threshold.

title: PHASES
subtitle: Mean 1-year rupture risk 1.4%; 5-year risk 3.4% (230 ruptures)

title: INVICTUS
subtitle: VKA SUPERIOR: restricted mean survival 1599 d (rivaroxaban) vs 1675 d (VKA)

title: WAKE-UP
subtitle: Favored alteplase: 53.3% vs 41.8%

title: TWIST
subtitle: No significant benefit overall

title: Jefferson Inherited Thrombophilia Audit
subtitle: HIGH ABNORMAL RATE, ZERO MANAGEMENT IMPACT. 42.2% of patients had at least one abnormal test and 14.3% of the 1035 individual tests resulted abnormal — but 28% of abnormal results were borderline positive antigen or activity assays that likely represented false positives, and NO patient with an abnormal result had their clinical management changed as a result. Charges for the tests totalled $468,588 USD.

title: sifap
subtitle: LOW BUT NON-TRIVIAL YIELD: definite Fabry disease was diagnosed in 0.5% (95% CI 0.4%-0.8%, n=27) of all patients, with probable Fabry disease in a further 18 patients (0.4%). Roughly 1 in 200 young stroke patients had definite Fabry disease. The figure depends on the study's own definite-versus-probable classification algorithm, so it is best used as an order-of-magnitude prevalence rather than a precise rate.

title: UKYSS
subtitle: Among ischemic strokes, 50.8% (723) were undetermined/cryptogenic; hypertension was a risk factor in 38.1% (542), not an etiologic classification. IV thrombolysis was used in 191 (13.4%) and EVT in 71 (5%). Among hemorrhagic strokes, hypertension was a risk factor in 56.6% and an assigned etiology in 49.6%; 15.3% underwent neurosurgery.

title: Illicit Drug Use and Stroke (meta-analysis + Mendelian randomization)
subtitle: POSITIVE for three of four drug classes: cannabis OR 1.37 (95% CI 1.14-1.65), cocaine OR 1.96 (95% CI 1.27-3.01) and amphetamines OR 2.22 (95% CI 1.40-3.53) were each significantly associated with increased stroke risk, while opioids showed NO significant association. The authors state explicitly that the cannabis finding showed heterogeneity and small-study effects, so it is the least secure of the three.

title: AFib Anticoagulation Restart Timing
subtitle: Randomized evidence on DOAC initiation after AF-related ischemic stroke, with trial-specific eligibility, hemorrhagic transformation and current-label dosing context.

title: Anticoagulation Reversal in Acute Hemorrhage
subtitle: Agent-specific reversal for intracranial hemorrhage, the FDA andexanet safety update and US sales cessation, PCC-based factor Xa reversal, and the distinct thrombolysis-associated hemorrhage pathway, with parallel BP and neurosurgical assessment.

title: Antiepileptic Drugs & Post-Stroke Seizures
subtitle: Clinical classification of post-stroke seizures, guideline-directed management, comparison of first-line and second-line antiseizure medications (ASMs), and post-stroke epilepsy risk stratification with the SeLECT score.

title: Basilar Artery Occlusion
subtitle: Protean brainstem presentation, the ATTENTION/BAOCHE evidence arc for endovascular therapy, imaging selection (pc-ASPECTS, perfusion/collaterals), and pitfalls for basilar artery occlusion.

title: Brain Death / BD-DNC
subtitle: Consensus guidelines for the determination of Brain Death / Death by Neurologic Criteria (BD/DNC) in adult and pediatric patients.

title: Brainstem Stroke Syndromes Atlas
subtitle: The crossed-deficit localization rule and the classic brainstem stroke syndromes (Wallenberg, Dejerine, Millard-Gubler, Foville, one-and-a-half, Weber, Benedikt, Claude) by level, vessel, and deficit.

title: Genetic Cerebral Small Vessel Vasculopathies (CADASIL, CARASIL, Fabry, MELAS, COL4A1)
subtitle: Molecular genetics, neuroimaging hallmarks (anterior temporal pole & external capsule hyperintensities, pulvinar sign), clinical phenotypes, and management pitfalls for monogenic stroke syndromes.

title: Cancer-Associated Stroke, Hypercoagulability & Marantic Endocarditis (NBTE)
subtitle: Pathophysiology of cancer-mediated hypercoagulability, 3-territory sign on DWI, markedly elevated D-dimer (no single validated cutoff; e.g., >3 µg/mL in the Schwarzbach DWI-phenotype cohort), non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE), and LMWH vs DOAC management.

title: Carotid Stenosis: Revascularization vs Medical Therapy
subtitle: Symptomatic vs asymptomatic carotid stenosis, NASCET measurement, CEA vs CAS (CREST), the CREST-2 asymptomatic results, and intensive medical therapy as the common foundation.

title: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis (CVST)
subtitle: Presentation, risk factors, venography-based diagnosis, anticoagulation despite venous hemorrhage, DOAC transition, and prognosis for cerebral venous and dural sinus thrombosis.

title: Cervical Artery Dissection
subtitle: Clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, medical management (extracranial vs. intracranial), and landmark trial evidence (CADISS, TREAT-CAD, STOP-CAD, and 2024 IPD meta-analysis) for cervical artery dissection.

title: Cryptogenic Stroke & ESUS Diagnostic Evaluation
subtitle: Embolic Stroke of Undetermined Source (ESUS) definition, empirical DOAC failure in unselected ESUS (NAVIGATE ESUS, RE-SPECT ESUS), biomarker-defined atrial cardiopathy trial analysis (ARCADIA), insertable cardiac monitor (ICM) yields (CRYSTAL AF, STROKE-AF), and stepwise diagnostic algorithm.

title: DAPT for Non-Cardioembolic Ischemic Stroke
subtitle: Guideline-directed Dual Antiplatelet Therapy (DAPT) for secondary non-cardioembolic stroke prevention.

title: Device-Detected & Subclinical AF
subtitle: Whether to anticoagulate an atrial high-rate episode found on a pacemaker, ICD, CRT device or insertable cardiac monitor: duration bands, mandatory electrogram adjudication, NOAH-AFNET 6 vs ARTESiA, the pooled meta-analysis, and absolute-risk framing.

title: Distal Medium Vessel Occlusions (DMVO/MeVO)
subtitle: Evaluation, anatomical classification (M2/M3, A2/A3, P2/P3), trial evidence (DISTAL, ESCAPE-MeVO), disabling deficit thresholds, microcatheter techniques, and perforation risk management.

title: External Ventricular Drain
subtitle: Concept reference on EVD measurement context, device-specific safety and individualized management. Operational steps, downloadable procedural sheet and simulation are unavailable.

title: EVT Technique & Post-Thrombectomy Care
subtitle: Anesthesia, procedural evidence and individualized post-EVT care, including the distinction between an active BP target, spontaneous pressure and newer selected-strategy evidence.

title: Fibromuscular Dysplasia & Cervical Artery Dissection
subtitle: Pathophysiology, angiographic classification (multifocal string-of-beads vs. focal), brain-to-pelvis vascular screening, and cervical artery dissection trials (CADISS, TREAT-CAD, STOP-CAD, Kaufmann IPD).

title: Intracranial Hypertension & Herniation - Stroke
subtitle: Concept reference on cerebral edema, herniation and escalation assessment. Drug recipes, the osmotherapy calculator and device simulation are unavailable.

title: HINTS+ Reference
subtitle: Written HINTS+ finding examples and a qualified pattern checklist for trained examiners assessing an appropriate acute vestibular syndrome. Eye-movement animations are unavailable.

title: Acute ICH Blood Pressure & Expansion Mitigation
subtitle: Population-specific ICH blood-pressure evidence, INTERACT3 bundle limitations, expansion-mitigation trials and surgical assessment. Infusion titration requires a complete monitored prescription.

title: ICH Surgical Decision-Making
subtitle: Trial-specific evidence for hematoma evacuation, selected minimally invasive surgery, decompression and urgent cerebellar-ICH assessment; observational associations and prognosis limits are explicit.

title: Intracranial Atherosclerotic Disease
subtitle: Mechanism-first diagnosis and treatment of symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis — artery-to-artery embolism, branch atheromatous perforator occlusion and hemodynamic borderzone failure; the SAMMPRIS aggressive medical bundle; and why stenting (SAMMPRIS, CASSISS), bypass for symptomatic atherosclerotic ICA/MCA occlusive disease (CMOSS, COSS, EC/IC 1985) and bailout angioplasty (ANGEL-REBOOT) all failed their primary endpoints.

title: Large-Core Thrombectomy
subtitle: Endovascular thrombectomy for large ischemic core (low ASPECTS or large core volume) — the six 2022–2024 RCTs, functional-outcome benefit, and the hemorrhage trade-off (more any intracranial hemorrhage and numerically higher sICH in most individual trials, but no significant sICH difference in the 2026 ATLAS IPD meta-analysis).

title: Malignant Infarction & Decompression
subtitle: Decompressive hemicraniectomy selection criteria, evidence, and supportive ICU care for malignant MCA syndrome.

title: Metabolic & Vascular Risk Modulation
subtitle: Comprehensive metabolic and vascular risk modulation in stroke prevention — GLP-1 receptor agonists (SELECT, FLOW, SUSTAIN-6), SGLT2 inhibitors, blood pressure lowering (SPRINT and RESPECT intensive targets; TRIDENT low-dose triple pill after ICH), MASH/obesity management, and the secondary prevention ABCDE bundle.

title: Moyamoya Disease & Moyamoya Syndrome: Medical & Surgical Revascularization
subtitle: Suzuki angiographic staging (1–6), direct STA-MCA bypass vs indirect EDAS/EMS, landmark JAM randomized trial for hemorrhagic Moyamoya, and strict perioperative hemodynamic/normocarbia protocols.

title: PFO Closure for Cryptogenic Stroke
subtitle: Who benefits from patent foramen ovale closure after a nonlacunar stroke of undetermined cause — the four randomized trials that showed benefit (CLOSE, RESPECT long-term, REDUCE, DEFENSE-PFO; the earlier CLOSURE I and PC trials were neutral), candidate selection with the RoPE score and PASCAL classification, the closure-vs-antiplatelet-vs-anticoagulation decision per the 2021 AHA/ASA and 2024 ESO guidelines, and the device-associated atrial fibrillation trade-off.

title: Post-Stroke Recovery, Cognition & Mood
subtitle: Owns the recovery phase — prognosis and the sensitive window (CPASS, PREP2, AVERT), the rehabilitation setting and dose decision (LEAPS, ICARE, EXCITE), the settled negative fluoxetine question (FOCUS, AFFINITY, EFFECTS) versus the positive paired vagus nerve stimulation trial (VNS-REHAB), aphasia therapy intensity, and screening for post-stroke cognitive impairment, depression, fatigue and spasticity.

title: Prehospital Triage & Stroke Systems of Care
subtitle: Deciding where the ambulance goes and how patients move between hospitals — mothership vs drip-and-ship and how to compute a local crossover, the neutral RACECAT result with its intracerebral hemorrhage harm signal, TRIAGE-STROKE, mobile stroke units (BEST-MSU, B_PROUD), why INTERACT4 does not support undifferentiated prehospital blood-pressure lowering, prehospital LVO scales (RACE, LAMS, C-STAT, FAST-ED), and door-in-door-out as the governing interfacility transfer metric.

title: Pupillometry & NPi Evidence
subtitle: Observational pupillometry evidence and its limits, including ORANGE and ischemic-stroke cohorts. Simulation and automatic patient-specific interpretation are unavailable.

title: Reversible Cerebral Vasoconstriction Syndrome (RCVS)
subtitle: Recurrent thunderclap headache, triggers, reversible segmental vasoconstriction, the RCVS² score to distinguish RCVS from PACNS, and management (calcium-channel blockers, avoid steroids).

title: SeLECT Post-Stroke Seizure Risk
subtitle: SeLECT score for predicting 1-year and 5-year risk of late post-stroke seizures and epilepsy after ischemic stroke.

title: Neurocritical Care of Severe Stroke
subtitle: Supportive and systemic levers in severe stroke: fever and targeted normothermia, airway and tracheostomy timing, edema pharmacotherapy, glucose, dysphagia and nutrition, VTE prophylaxis, and mobilization dose.

title: Stroke Core Measures
subtitle: Reference guide for Joint Commission / GWTG stroke core measures and Comprehensive Stroke Center (CSC) quality metrics.

title: Stroke Prognosis & Clinical Scores
subtitle: Clinical prognostic models for acute stroke: ASTRAL and PLAN scores for ischemic stroke, and the ICH Score for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage.

title: TOAST Stroke Classification
subtitle: Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) diagnostic criteria for ischemic stroke etiology.

title: Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysm: Rupture Risk vs Treatment Risk
subtitle: Counseling an incidental unruptured intracranial aneurysm: separating symptomatic from truly incidental presentations, quantifying 5-year rupture risk with PHASES (and its limits), the ISUIA and UCAS Japan natural-history data, ELAPSS growth prediction, the procedural-risk side of the ledger (endovascular vs neurosurgical), and a surveillance protocol with scripts for the two hard conversations.

title: Cerebral Vascular Territory & Watershed Atlas
subtitle: Anterior (ACA/MCA/lenticulostriate/anterior-choroidal) and posterior (PCA/PICA/AICA/SCA/basilar-perforator) territories with their clinical signatures, plus cortical and internal watershed patterns and mechanisms.

title: High-Resolution Vessel Wall MRI (VW-MRI) Differential
subtitle: High-resolution black-blood vessel wall MRI differential matrix for intracranial arteriopathies — distinguishing ICAD, Primary CNS Vasculitis (PACNS), RCVS, Arterial Dissection, and Moyamoya disease via wall morphology, enhancement patterns, and remodeling.
